title: Reservoir fusion + kernel-affinity scheduler to stabilize embedding p99
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Background: Recent production runs show intermittent p99 spikes for the embeddings endpoint under mixed-size loads (singletons + bulk queries). Existing micro-batching reduces avg cost but leaves a long tail when a small number of large-sequence requests interleave with many small ones. This ticket implements a probabilistic reservoir-fusion ingress buffer with kernel-affinity hints to flatten the p99 while preserving single-request latency for critical customers. Goals: (1) reduce embed p99 by >=45% for mixed workloads, (2) keep median within +/-10% of current baseline, (3) avoid >5% regression for single-request P50 latency. Deliver a canary, automated rollout, and dashboarding for regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Canary traffic (10% of a single region) shows >=45% reduction in p99 for synthetic mixed workload (50k qps equivalent with size distribution skewed to 80% small, 20% large)
No more than 5% increase in P50 for single-request latency on canary
Scheduler exposes two new config knobs: reservoir_size and fusion_probability; both have defaults and safe upper bounds
Kernel-affinity hinting integrated with runtime kernel selector and observable in trace spans
Automated rollback if p95 regressions >10% or error-rate increase >0.1% within 30m interval
technical_notes: Design summary: introduce a per-worker reservoir queue (bounded ring) that probabilistically holds small requests for up to 8ms to opportunistically fuse them with nearby requests. Fusion is stochastic: each incoming request has chance p to be retained and fused; p adapts based on recent qps and token budget. When sequences exceed a size threshold, scheduler tags request with kernel_affinity=large_seq; kernel selector will prefer kernels optimized for long sequences (pre-warmed quantized kernels) and avoid CPU fallback. Implementation touches: ingress (proxy) to propagate fusion hints, worker scheduler to manage reservoir and fusion window, kernel-selection API changes to accept affinity hints, metrics and traces for reservoir hits/misses and fusion latency. Memory and per-worker state: reservoir default size 64 entries; each entry stores 64B of metadata. Trade-offs: adds small (ms) queuing for some requests, complexity in bursty patterns, needs backpressure integration with tenant-rate-limiter. Detailed algorithms and pseudo-code in linked design doc.
experiment_plan: Spike (2w): implement reservoir queue + basic fusion logic behind feature flag; unit tests and microbenchmarks on dev-gpu cluster
Bench (1w): run synthetic mixed-size workloads with and without fusion, capture token throughput, p50/p95/p99, and headroom for kernel warm paths
Canary (1w): enable for 10% traffic in us-west-2; monitor dashboards and automated checks; collect real-customer traces
Rollout (3w): progressive ramp to 100% with auto-escalation gates; instrument rollback triggers and add runtime config defaults
results_so_far: Spike implemented on branch feat/reservoir-fusion (GH: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4123). Microbench on rtxA40 shows p99 down from 420ms -> 195ms for 80/20 mixed workload (512-dim embeddings).
Observed 1.8% increase in median for singleton latency in bench; within target but needs validation on real traffic
Kernel-affinity flag added to trace spans; initial tests prefer fast long-seq kernels and avoid quant fallback in 92% of large requests
Memory overhead per worker measured at +1.3MB with reservoir_size=64; within node budget
decisions: Use stochastic fusion rather than fixed-delay aggregation to reduce worst-case queueing and keep single-request latency low
Set default reservoir_size=64 and max_hold_ms=8 after microbench trade-offs between p99 improvement and p50 regression
Kernel-affinity implemented as best-effort hint; kernel selector keeps final authority to avoid unsafe kernel switches
Expose fusion_probability and reservoir_size as runtime-configurable fields in Console and per-tenant overrides
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Fusion could increase tail if misconfigured during traffic burst. Mitigation: conservative defaults, adaptive p that decays to 0 under high queue occupancy, and circuit-breaker in scheduler.
Risk: Added scheduler complexity could regress throughput on small nodes. Mitigation: microbench for smallest instance types, and an opt-out flag for small-instance customers.
Risk: Kernel affinity might choose suboptimal kernels for model variants. Mitigation: add telemetry to score kernel selection and auto-fallback on observed perf regressions
